title: 13 Steps to Mentalism
subtitle: Tony Corinda
description: A foundational reference compiling core mentalism techniques—psychological and physical forces, muscle reading, prediction effects, and memory demonstrations—originally issued as a correspondence course and still used to teach the craft's fundamentals.

title: Practical Mental Effects
subtitle: Theodore Annemann
description: A collection of mentalism routines from one of the field's most influential creators, built around psychological misdirection and audience management rather than any claim of real mind reading.

title: Tricks of the Mind
subtitle: Derren Brown
description: Brown explains, in plain terms, the suggestion, misdirection, memory, and cold-reading techniques behind his stage and TV performances, explicitly framing them as psychological skill rather than supernatural ability.

title: Pure Effect: Direct Mindreading and Magical Techniques
subtitle: Derren Brown
description: A technical text for performers on constructing convincing 'mind-reading' effects through scripting, psychological forcing, and stagecraft rather than sleight of hand.

title: Psychological Subtleties
subtitle: Banachek
description: A widely used series in the mentalism community detailing subtle verbal and behavioral techniques—psychological forces, equivoque, and reading reactions—for steering a spectator's choices without their awareness.

title: Magic and Showmanship: A Handbook for Conjurors
subtitle: Henning Nelms
description: A classic analysis of performance psychology for magicians, covering how attention is directed and held, and why technically sound tricks still fail without deliberate audience management.

title: Prism
subtitle: Max Maven
description: A career-spanning collection from one of mentalism's most scholarly performers, covering prediction structures and dual-reality methods with detailed notes on the reasoning behind each effect.

title: Stunners!!
subtitle: Larry Becker
description: A practical mentalism text focused on high-impact prediction and thought-revelation routines, with an emphasis on constructing effects that feel personally meaningful to the spectator.

title: The Full Facts Book of Cold Reading
subtitle: Ian Rowland
description: The standard technical manual on cold reading, breaking the technique into its component parts (Barnum statements, feedback reading, shotgunning) purely as a performance and persuasion skill, with an explicit rejection of any real psychic claim.

title: The Secrets of Conjuring and Magic
subtitle: Jean-Eugène Robert-Houdin
description: An early foundational text by the performer often called the father of modern conjuring, whose ideas about misdirection and audience attention still underpin how mentalism and magic are taught today.

title: Derren Brown
subtitle: Mentalist, author, and television performer
description: Known for stage and television work built on suggestion, misdirection, and showmanship, Brown is unusual among performers for writing at length about exactly how his effects work rather than protecting the mystery.

title: Banachek (Steve Shaw)
subtitle: Professional mentalist and originator of widely taught psychological forcing methods
description: Beyond his performance work, Banachek was one of two young magicians in the 1979-1981 'Project Alpha' sting organized with skeptic James Randi, which used deceptive 'psychic' demonstrations to expose weak protocols in parapsychology research.

title: Max Maven
subtitle: Mentalist and historian of mental magic
description: Beyond his own performing career, Maven was widely sought as a creative consultant and historian for other magicians and television productions, and was known for unusually rigorous written analysis of why mentalism effects work.

title: Ian Rowland
subtitle: Cold-reading researcher and professional mentalist
description: Rowland systematized cold reading into a teachable technique and has separately worked with skeptics' organizations to explain how ostensibly psychic readings are constructed, treating the subject as applied psychology rather than the paranormal.

title: Kenton Knepper
subtitle: Mentalist and author on conversational scripting techniques
description: Knepper writes about how ordinary conversational language can be structured to guide a listener's attention and assumptions, a scripting approach widely referenced in modern mentalism routines.

title: Attention and Misdirection Research
description: Neuroscientists Stephen Macknik and Susana Martinez-Conde published peer-reviewed work (including in Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2008) analyzing how magicians' misdirection techniques exploit real limits of visual attention and awareness, treating stage technique as a source of genuine cognitive-science data.

title: Cold Reading Technique
description: The study of how vague, high-probability statements combined with attentive feedback reading can feel personally specific to a listener; it draws on the Barnum/Forer effect first demonstrated experimentally by psychologist Bertram Forer in 1949.

title: Suggestion and Indirect Language
description: Research and clinical writing on indirect suggestion, most associated with psychiatrist Milton Erickson, examines how language structure alone can shape a listener's expectations and responses—concepts mentalists borrow for scripting.

title: Memory and Expert Performance
description: Research into memory athletes and the method of loci, along with K. Anders Ericsson's broader studies of trained expert performance, explains how demonstrations that look like extraordinary memory are built from learnable, structured techniques.

title: Choice Blindness
description: A real experimental finding, first published by Petter Johansson and colleagues in Science (2005), showing that people will confidently justify a choice they did not actually make once it is covertly swapped—closely relevant to how psychological forcing can go undetected.
